transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… hi. I guess I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping my thoughts together when I talk. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but I’ll start telling someone about an overnight shift and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts, and people look like they’ve completely lost me. I know that’s not ideal. I just… I can’t keep my words in a straight line lately, if that makes sense.
Have you been using any alcohol or drugs recently?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I’m not doing drugs or anything like that. Alcohol… I don’t think it’s anything worth mentioning. I can’t really point to that as the reason for all this, if that’s what you mean.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty keeping your thoughts together?

I guess it’s been… longer than I want to make it sound. Maybe about a year and five months? It kind of started after my job changed from regular day shifts to rotating nights and a lot of overtime. I thought I was just adjusting badly, or tired, but it’s kept going.
Have you been experiencing any hallucinations, like seeing or hearing things that aren't really there?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like seeing people who aren’t there or hearing voices talking to me, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I’m really tired and I might misread a sound or think someone called me, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound like something it isn’t. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but most days I wake up feeling really heavy, kind of empty. I try to push through and act normal, but after shifts sometimes I just sit in my car and cry for a while before I can even drive home. Is that… is that what you mean by depressed?
Have you been feeling anxious or overly worried about things lately?

I’m… not sure. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess, like whether I’m doing things right or if people are upset with me, but I don’t know if it’s “overly” worried. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. What would count as too much?
Do you often find yourself worrying about things to the point where it interferes with your daily activities?

I… I don’t know if I’d say it interferes a lot. I mean, I still get up and go to work and do what I’m supposed to do. Sometimes I get stuck thinking about whether I messed something up or said the wrong thing, and it can make it harder to focus, but… I’m not sure if that counts as interfering. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy, energetic, or irritable, and your thoughts were racing?

I don’t think so… not like extremely happy or energized. I get irritable sometimes, but I think that’s normal, like when I’m tired or stressed. My thoughts can feel busy, but I wouldn’t want to say “racing” if that means something more specific. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless or have trouble relaxing when you're not working or actively doing something?

Yeah… sometimes. I try to just sit and relax, but I end up pacing around my apartment or rubbing my hands together without really thinking about it, and then I notice they’re kind of sore.

But then other times it’s the opposite, I guess. People have told me I’m moving really slow, like… like I’m underwater or something. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean. Is that helpful?
Have you ever felt extremely happy or energized for a period of time?

Not really, no. I mean… I’ve had better days where I’m in a decent mood or I get through work okay, but I wouldn’t say extremely happy or full of energy for a while. If that’s what you’re asking, I don’t think I’ve had that. Is that okay?
Do you find that you worry about things more days than not?
I’m not really sure… I mean, I worry sometimes, like anyone does, but I don’t know if it’s more days than not. I haven’t really kept track of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you usually worry about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

I don’t think so… not usually. I mean, if something’s actually going on, yeah, I’ll worry some, but just out of nowhere for no reason? I haven’t really noticed that. Maybe I’m not paying close enough attention, though. Is that answer okay?
Do you often worry about everyday things like work, finances, or relationships?

I mean… I worry about that stuff sometimes, yeah, like work or money, but I don’t know if I’d say “often.” It doesn’t feel like it’s all the time or anything. Relationships… not really, I guess. I might be missing what you mean by often, though. Is that answer alright?
Do you usually find yourself worrying about things even when everything in your life seems to be going well?

If things are actually going well, I don’t think I’m usually sitting there worrying, no. I might still have little thoughts here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s a big pattern… at least not that I’ve really noticed. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your worrying is something that you've been doing for as long as you can remember, or is it something that has started more recently?

I’m not really sure… I don’t think it’s been like a lifelong thing, at least not that I can remember. It kind of just depends on what’s going on. I haven’t really tracked it, though, so I might not be the best judge. Is that okay?
Do you think you worry more than other people do about everyday things?

I don’t think so… I mean, I guess everybody worries about work and bills and stuff, right? I don’t really know how much other people worry, so it’s hard to compare. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you've been worrying almost every day for the past six months?

I don’t think it’s been almost every day for six months, no… or at least I haven’t noticed it like that. I mean, I worry when there’s something to worry about, but I wouldn’t say it’s constant. I hope that answers it the right way.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most days for the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days lately I wake up feeling really heavy, like empty inside. And after my shifts, sometimes I just sit in my car and cry for a while before I can even drive home. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like your worries have been interfering with your daily life for a long time?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it has interfered more than I’d like to admit. At work I’ve needed coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting, because I don’t trust myself not to mess something up. And at home I’ve kind of let things slide—bills, answering friends, my apartment getting really bad.

I didn’t want to make it sound like I can’t handle things, but… it got serious enough that employee health had me go for an emergency evaluation after I told them I was thinking about suicide. Is that what you mean by interfering?
Do you think your worrying has been a consistent part of your life for more than six months?

I’m not sure I’d call it consistent for more than six months. I mean, I’ve worried about things, sure, but I haven’t really kept track of it like that, and I don’t want to say yes if that’s not accurate. It feels more like it comes up around certain things, if that makes sense.
